newsitem.title: CHINA: China ambassador tells North Korea friendship firm.
newsitem.headline: China ambassador tells North Korea friendship firm.

text.p: China said on Thursday its policy of friendship with its communist ally North Korea was firm and unshakable.
The message was relayed as Beijing's newly appointed ambassador in Pyongyang, Wan Yongxiang, presented his credentials.

"It is the firm and unshakable policy of the Communist Party of China and the Chinese government to consolidate and develop the traditional friendship with the Democratic People's Republic of Korea," Xinhua news agnecy quoted Wan as saying.
North Korean Vice President Li Jong-ok replied his country would strive to consolidate and develop friendship with China, Xinhua said in a report from Pyongyang.
"The friendship between the two countries is developing continuously with the solicitude of the parties and governments...," Xinhua quoted Li as saying.
China's relations with North Korea were sorely tested when senior Pyongyang official Hwang Jang-yop sought asylum in South Korea's diplomatic mission in Beijing in February.
Hwang was allowed to leave for the Philippines after a standoff that lasted nearly five weeks.

Beijing was so unsure of its communist ally's possible response that it stationed armoured personnel carriers to guard Hwang and posted police outside the North Korean embassy to keep a watchful eye on its comrade in arms.
China fought alongside the North in the 1950-53 Korean War but it has been forced to balance ties to its old communist ally with new friendship for the capitalist South.
Beijing also offered what appeared to be thinly veiled criticism of the North's hardline Stalinist policies which have left that nation isolated and impoverished.

China's ambassador was quoted as expressing hope that North Korea would achieve new successes in the struggle for the economic development and the improvement of living standards as well as its stated goal of reunification with the South.
